html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Operating Cycle Analysis

Orion Company reports the following information for the current year. Analyze receivables, inventory, credit losses, and operating cash flow.

Financial Information

  • Beginning Accounts Receivable: $180,000
  • Ending Accounts Receivable before year-end credit-loss adjustment: $220,000
  • Sales revenue on account: $900,000
  • Allowance for Credit Losses has a $3,000 debit balance before adjustment.
  • Required ending Allowance for Credit Losses: $16,000 credit balance
  • Beginning Inventory: $140,000
  • Purchases: $500,000
  • Ending Inventory: $170,000
  • Net income after all accrual-basis year-end adjustments, including the credit-loss adjustment: $210,000
  • Depreciation expense: $35,000
  • Accounts Payable increased by: $20,000

Item 1 — Cash Collected from Customers

How much cash was collected from customers during the year?

Item 2 — Credit Loss Expense

What credit loss expense must be recognized to produce the required ending allowance?

Item 3 — Cost of Goods Sold

What is cost of goods sold for the year?

Item 4 — Inventory Adjustment in CFO

Under the indirect method, what adjustment related to Inventory should be made to net income?

Enter the adjustment as a positive amount if added to net income or a negative amount if subtracted.

Item 5 — Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities

Using the indirect method, calculate net cash provided by operating activities.
explanation:
Item 1 — Cash Collected

Use the Accounts Receivable rollforward.

Beginning Accounts Receivable: $180,000

+ Credit Sales: $900,000

− Cash Collections

= Ending Accounts Receivable: $220,000

Cash Collections = $860,000

Item 2 — Credit Loss Expense

The Allowance for Credit Losses has a $3,000 debit balance before adjustment and must end with a $16,000 credit balance.

Required ending credit balance: $16,000

+ Existing debit balance: $3,000

Credit Loss Expense = $19,000

Item 3 — Cost of Goods Sold

Beginning Inventory: $140,000

+ Purchases: $500,000

− Ending Inventory: $170,000

Cost of Goods Sold = $470,000

Item 4 — Inventory CFO Adjustment

Inventory increased from $140,000 to $170,000.

Ending Inventory: $170,000

− Beginning Inventory: $140,000

= Increase in Inventory: $30,000

Because inventory increased, it is subtracted from net income under the indirect method.

CFO Adjustment = −$30,000

Item 5 — Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities

Net Income: $210,000

+ Depreciation Expense: $35,000

− Increase in Accounts Receivable: $40,000

− Increase in Inventory: $30,000

+ Increase in Accounts Payable: $20,000

Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities = $195,000

Key FAR Relationships

An increase in Accounts Receivable decreases operating cash flow under the indirect method.

An increase in Inventory decreases operating cash flow.

An increase in Accounts Payable increases operating cash flow.
